decision: Do not introduce native planning/reconsider schema in this delta; retain valid examples and typed diagnostics. No semantic or live reliability improvement is claimed.

observations.finding: Both use the existing research.reasoning._ask_model without response_schema; preparation already passes native schemas for its two calls.

parameters accepts an arbitrary finite JSON object, including nested objects/lists and typed booleans/numbers. Omission of nonapplicable effect_type is valid; supplied null is rejected. Capability, target and authority cannot be inferred to fill a declaration.
Existing adapters forward json_schema with strict=True and do not transform a planning schema. They do not provide an adapter capability negotiation for open parameter maps.

The installed SDK strict-schema helper makes every declared object property required and adds additionalProperties=False when absent. ORA passes a raw schema instead of invoking this helper. This is local source evidence of the strict shape expected by that SDK, not a live API rejection test.

The installed response_json_schema documentation includes anyOf/oneOf/properties/additionalProperties/required. The SDK transport accepts an arbitrary schema object, which does not attest cross-provider server acceptance.
Existing SDK and HTTP-fake tests exercise transport of a closed schema with required fields. They do not prove remote acceptance of a union with optional effects and open parameters.

concrete_risks: Closing parameters to match the preparation schema would reject or lose currently valid capability parameters, including cursor/version and owned-write values.
Adding null to the effect_type enum as an optional-field surrogate would conflict with the unchanged runtime validator.
Using optional/open objects directly with strict=True is not established compatible by the current fake-HTTP tests.
Changing parameter representation, negotiating provider features or enumerating capability-specific parameter schemas would exceed the minimal two-callsite supplement.

legacy_travel_test.finding: Its positive fixture obtains a web_search snippet about five hours and expects a two-decision personal travel estimate. web_search returns kind=tool and explicitly qualifies snippets as not live traffic/routing APIs; the empirical guard accepts research observations or the existing direct estimators, not web_search alone.
legacy_travel_test.scope_limit: The saved failure log has no complete tool observation. Search availability is also checked before the mocked _failover_search, so the exact first failure boundary is not independently distinguished by that log. Even a successful snippet would not satisfy the current empirical-estimate contract.
legacy_travel_test.action: Keep test unchanged and document this nonintroduced incompatibility. A replacement direct-route fixture would require explicit test-contract changes (personal capability, current ETA, provider-call assertion); it is not a safe one-line snippet fix.

next_step: Freeze. Review the peer diagnostic wrapper after its owner declares the patch stable.
